brief: How I redesigned my workday around energy, not hours — 5 quiet shifts.

slots.subtitle: Five quiet shifts that redesigned my workday around focus, rest, and honest output.
slots.author: Slow Foundry
Slow Foundry
slots.body: I stopped glorifying busy. Now I track output by clarity, not by how long my laptop stays open.

slots.author: Slow Foundry
slots.body: I logged my focus for one week, then moved creative work to mid-morning when my brain actually fires.

slots.author: Slow Foundry
slots.body: I turned off all non-human notifications. The cost of interruption is higher than the guilt of being offline.

slots.author: Slow Foundry
slots.body: Emails and admin drain momentum. I cluster them at day's end so mornings stay sacred for thinking.

slots.author: Slow Foundry
slots.body: Lunch is no longer a task squeezed between calls. I block twenty minutes of stillness before the afternoon.

slots.author: Slow Foundry
slots.body: A ten-minute shutdown signals my brain to release the day. Work ends so life can actually begin.

slots.author: Slow Foundry
slots.body: Pick one shift to try this week. Small changes compound into a calmer, more sustainable work life.
